stepTypes.name: StartActivity
stepTypes.description: The StartActivity step may be used to start the next operation activity for an entity. Refer to the Operation and Activity elements to define an operation and its activities.

exits.name: The token exits the step from this exit point if there are no further operation activities to perform for the entity.

stepTypes.name: StartOperation
stepTypes.description: The StartOperation step may be used to start a new operation for an entity. Refer to the Operation element to define an operation.

properties.name: OperationName
properties.description: The name of the operation to start.

stepTypes.name: StartTasks
stepTypes.description: The StartTasks step may be used to initiate a task sequence that is associated with an object in the model. Refer to the Task Sequence element to define a task sequence.

properties.name: TaskSequenceName
properties.description: The name of the task sequence to start.

properties.name: ObjectType
properties.description: The object that the task sequence execution will be associated with. May be specified as either the object associated with the executing token, the parent object, or as a specific object reference.

properties.name: Object
properties.description: The specific object that the task sequence execution will be associated with.

properties.name: RandomNumberStream
properties.description: The random number stream to be used if there is probabilistic branching in the task sequence.

properties.name: TokenWaitAction
properties.description:
The wait action to be taken by the token arriving to the StartTasks step.

If the action is 'NoWait', then the token will immediately exit the step after starting the specified task sequence.

stepTypes.name: Stipulate
stepTypes.description: The Stipulate step may be used to add dependencies and requirements that entities must satisfy before proceeding.

properties.name: StipulationType
properties.description:
The kind of stipulation being applied to the 'Candidate Entity':

'NodeListRoutingDependency' will prevent the entity from routing through a specific node list until the 'Entity to Follow' has routed through first.

'ResourceAllocationDependency' will prevent the entity from seizing a specific resource (or seizing from a specific resource list) until the 'Entity to Follow' has seized the resource (or seized from the resource list) first.

'NodeListRequirement' will force the entity to select a specific node from a node list, overriding whatever node selection rule would normally be used.

'ResourceListRequirement' will force the entity to select a specific resource from a resource list, overriding whatever resource selection rule would normally be used.

properties.name: Entity
properties.description: The name of the entity affected by this stipulation.

properties.name: NodeList
properties.description: The name of the node list used by this dependency or requirement.

properties.name: ResourceOrList
properties.description: The name of the resource or resource list for this resource allocation dependency.  The 'Candidate Entity' will not proceed until the 'Entity to Follow' has seized the specified resource, or seized from the specified resource list, 'Prior Usage Count' times.

properties.name: EntityToFollow
properties.description: The name of the entity that must proceed through the specified resource, resource list, or node list, before the candidate entity may proceed.

properties.name: PriorUsageCount
properties.description: Specifies the number of times the 'Entity to Follow' must seize the resource, seize from the resource list, or be routed through the node list, before the 'Candidate Entity' may proceed.  The default value is 1.

properties.name: RequiredNode
properties.description: Identifies the specific node in the node list that the 'Candidate Entity' must select.

properties.name: ResourceList
properties.description: The name of the resource list used by this requirement.

properties.name: RequiredResource
properties.description: Identifies the specific resource in the resource list that the 'Candidate Entity' must seize.

properties.name: RoutingGroup
properties.description: An optional reference to the routing group that must be used by the candidate entity for this node stipulation to apply

properties.name: SeizeLocation
properties.description: An optional reference to an object the owner making the seize must be located at for this resource stipulation to apply

stepTypes.name: Subscribe
stepTypes.description: The Subscribe step may be used to add a new triggering event for a process, so that the process is executed whenever the event occurs. Use the UnSubscribe step to cancel a triggering event for a process.

properties.name: EventName
properties.description: The name of the triggering event to add.

properties.name: EventCondition
properties.description: Optional condition to be evaluated whenever the triggering event occurs, and which must be true to cause the execution of the specified process.

properties.name: ProcessName
properties.description: The name of the process to execute.

properties.name: Events
properties.description: Additional triggering events to add.

stepTypes.name: Suspend
stepTypes.description: The Suspend step may be used to suspend various types of model behavior. The Resume step may then be later used to remove the suspension.

properties.name: SuspendType
properties.description: The type of behavior or logic to suspend.

properties.name: ProcessName
properties.description: The name of the process to suspend.

properties.name: TokenMatchCondition
properties.description:
Optional match condition used to filter the tokens executing the process. Only tokens currently in process that satisfy this condition will be suspended.

In the expression, use the syntax Candidate.[TokenClass].[Attribute] or Candidate.[TokenAssociatedObjectClass].[Attribute] to reference an attribute of either the candidate process tokens themselves or the objects associated with those process tokens (e.g., Candidate.Token.TimeInProcess or Candidate.Entity.TimeInSystem).

properties.name: ObjectType
properties.description: The object whose movement capability is to be suspended. May be specified as either the object associated with the executing token, the parent object, or as a specific object reference.

properties.name: Object
properties.description: The specific object whose movement capability is to be suspended.

properties.name: FlowRegulatorName
properties.description: The name of the regulator whose flow capability is to be suspended.

properties.name: BatchLogicName
properties.description: The name of the Batch Logic element to suspend.

properties.name: SuspendActions
properties.description: Additional suspend actions.

stepTypes.name: Tally
stepTypes.description: The Tally step records an observation value for a specified Tally Statistic element.

properties.name: TallyStatisticName
properties.description: The name of the tally statistic for which to record an observation value.

properties.name: ValueType
properties.description:
The type of observation value to record.

If the value type is 'Expression', then the value of the specified expression is recorded.

If the value type is 'TimeBetween', then the time since the last token arrival to this or any other Tally step referencing the tally statistic is recorded.

properties.name: ValueExpression
properties.description: The expression returning the value to be recorded.

properties.name: NumberOfObservations
properties.description: The number of observation values to record.

properties.name: Tallies
properties.description: Additional tallies.

stepTypes.name: Transfer
stepTypes.description: The Transfer step may be used to transfer an entity object between different types of locations.

properties.name: EntityType
properties.description: The entity object to be transferred. May be specified as either the object associated with the executing token, the parent object, or as a specific object reference.

properties.name: EntityObject
properties.description: The specific entity object to be transferred.

properties.name: FromType
properties.description: The location type from which the entity object is to be transferred.

properties.name: ToType
properties.description: The location type to which the entity object is to be transferred.

properties.name: NodeName
properties.description: The name of the node to which the entity is to be transferred.

properties.name: ExternalNodeName
properties.description: The name of the external node on the parent object to which the entity is to be transferred.

properties.name: StationName
properties.description: The name of the station into which the entity is to be transferred.

properties.name: ContainerName
properties.description: The name of the container into which the entity is to be transferred.

properties.name: FacilityName
properties.description: The object whose Facility window will contain the entity's free space location. If left unspecified, then defaults to the most immediate parent object of the Transfer step that supports a Facility window.

properties.name: OutboundLinkPreference
properties.description:
The preference used by the entity to select an outbound link from its current node to its next destination. 

If the preference is 'Default', then the outbound link preference settings for the entity's current node will be used.

If the preference is 'Any', then the specified Outbound Link Rule will be strictly adhered to and blocked outbound links may cause the entity to wait.

If the preference is 'Available', then the specified Outbound Link Rule will be automatically adjusted to minimize waiting time by first applying the rule only to outbound links that are immediately available for entry. If no outbound links are immediately available, then the preference will revert to 'Any' selection.

If the preference is 'Specific', then the entity will be transferred to the specified Outbound Link Name.

properties.name: OutboundLinkRule
properties.description:
The rule used by the entity to select an outbound link from its current node to its next destination. 

Note that if the rule is set to 'Shortest Path', and the entity does not have an assigned destination, then the rule will revert to 'By Link Weight' selection.

properties.name: OutboundLinkName
properties.description: The name of the specific outbound link that will be selected by the entity.

properties.name: FlowRegulatorName
properties.description: The regulator used if transferring the entity's mass and volume as a continuous flow into the new location.

properties.name: PathPlannerName
properties.description:
The name of the Path Planner element used by the entity to find and reserve a network deadlock-free shortest path from its current node to its destination node.

NOTE: If the Flow Regulator Name property is specified then the Path Planner Name property is ignored. If path planning is used by an entity then the Outbound Link Preference and Outbound Link Rule properties are ignored.

properties.name: RandomNumberStream
properties.description: The random number stream to be used if probabilistically selecting an outbound link from the node using the 'By Link Weight' selection rule.

properties.name: FailIfBlocked
properties.description: Indicates whether to fail (balk) the transfer attempt if the entity cannot immediately transfer into the desired location due to the location being full. If the transfer attempt fails, then the arriving token will immediately exit the 'Failed' exit point of the Transfer step.

properties.name: TokenWaitAction
properties.description: The wait action to be taken by the token arriving to the Transfer step.

stepTypes.name: Travel
stepTypes.description: The Travel step may be used to perform a movement of an entity in free space.

properties.name: EntityType
properties.description: The entity that is performing the free space travel movement. May be specified as either the object associated with the executing token, the parent object, or as a specific object reference.

properties.name: EntityObject
properties.description: The specific entity object that is performing the free space travel movement.

properties.name: SteeringBehavior
properties.description: The steering behavior of the entity during the free space travel movement.
allowedValues: Follow Network Path Same Network Object Avoidance

properties.name: TokenWaitAction
properties.description:
The wait action to be taken by the token arriving to the Travel step.

If the action is 'NoWait', then the token will immediately exit the step without waiting for completion of the free space travel movement.

stepTypes.name: UnBatch
stepTypes.description: The UnBatch step may be used to remove batch members from a specified parent entity. New tokens associated with the unbatched members will exit the 'Member' exit point of the step. Use the Batch step to add batch members.

properties.name: ParentEntityType
properties.description: The parent entity that is carrying the batch members. May be specified as either the object associated with the executing token, the parent object, or as a specific object reference.

properties.name: ParentEntityObject
properties.description: The specific parent entity object that is carrying the batch members.

properties.name: DesiredQuantity
properties.description: The desired number of batch members to remove (unbatch) from the parent entity.

properties.name: RemovalOrder
properties.description: The order in which to search for and remove batch members from the parent entity.

properties.name: MatchCondition
properties.description:
Optional match condition used to filter the batch member entities. Only entities that satisfy this condition will be removed from the batch.

In the expression, use the syntax Candidate.[EntityClass].[Attribute] to reference an attribute of the candidate entities (e.g., Candidate.Entity.Priority).

properties.name: OnEnteredFreeSpaceProcess
properties.description: Indicates whether or not to execute the built-in OnEnteredFreeSpace process for each unbatched member entity after it is removed from the parent entity’s batch members queue.

properties.name: TokenWaitAction
properties.description:
The wait action to be taken by the token arriving to the UnBatch step.

If the action is ‘NoWait’, then the execution of all new tokens associated with unbatched members will be scheduled on the simulation’s current events calendar as an early priority event. The original token will then immediately exit the step.

If the action is 'NewTokensExitFirst', then all new tokens associated with unbatched members will exit the step first before the original token exits.

If the action is 'WaitUntilNewTokenProcessingCompleted', then the original token will wait until the processing of all new tokens associated with unbatched members has been completed before exiting the step.

stepTypes.name: UnPark
stepTypes.description: The UnPark step may be used to transfer an entity object out of a node's parking station and into the node. Use the Park step to park an entity.

properties.name: EntityType
properties.description: The entity object to be unparked. May be specified as either the object associated with the executing token, the parent object, or as a specific object reference.

properties.name: EntityObject
properties.description: The specific entity object to be unparked.

properties.name: TokenWaitAction
properties.description: The wait action to be taken by the token arriving to the UnPark step.

stepTypes.name: UnReserve
stepTypes.description: The UnReserve step may be used to cancel reservations for resources or material stock made by a specified owner. Use the Reserve step to create a new resource or material stock reservation.

properties.name: OwnerType
properties.description: The object that owns the reservation(s) to be cancelled. May be specified as either the object associated with the executing token, the parent object, or as a specific object reference.

properties.name: OwnerObject
properties.description: The specific object that owns the reservation(s) to be cancelled.

properties.name: ReservationType
properties.description: Indicates whether to cancel a resource or material reservation.

properties.name: ResourceName
properties.description: The name of the resource object to unreserve.

properties.name: NumberCapacityUnits
properties.description: The desired number of capacity units of the resource to unreserve. Any existing reservations made by the owner object will be cancelled up to this maximum.

properties.name: MaterialConsumptionType
properties.description:
The type of material consumption.

Material – A single material.

BillOfMaterials – A list of component materials.

BillOfMaterialsGroup – Alternative lists of component materials.

properties.name: MaterialName
properties.description: The name of the material.

properties.name: InventorySiteType
properties.description: Indicates the fixed object that is the inventory location. Applies only to material elements whose Location Based Inventory property is set to True.

properties.name: InventorySiteObjectName
properties.description: The name of the fixed object that is the inventory location.

properties.name: BOMName
properties.description: The name of the bill of materials.

properties.name: BOMGroupName
properties.description: The name of the bill of materials group.

properties.name: MaterialQuantity
properties.description: The quantity of the material or parent assembly. Any existing reservations made by the owner object will be cancelled up to this maximum.

properties.name: MaterialLotID
properties.description: Optional string value indicating the lot identifier of the material or parent assembly.

properties.name: Reservations
properties.description: Additional reservations to cancel.

stepTypes.name: UnSetRow
stepTypes.description: The UnSetRow step may be used to remove table row references previously set for the executing token or a specified object or element. Use the SetRow step to set a table row reference.

properties.name: TableType
properties.description: Indicates the tables to remove the row references to. ‘All’ will remove all table row references previously set for the specified object or element.

properties.name: TableNames
properties.description: The names of the tables to remove the row references to.

properties.name: ObjectType
properties.description: The object for which to remove the specified table row references. May be specified as either the executing token, the object associated with the executing token, the parent object, or as a specific object or element reference.

properties.name: ObjectOrElement
properties.description: The specific object or element for which to remove the specified table row references.

properties.name: UnSetRowCondition
properties.description: Optional condition that, if specified, must evaluate to true to remove any table row references for the specified object or element.

stepTypes.name: UnSubscribe
stepTypes.description: The UnSubscribe step may be used to cancel a triggering event for a process, so that the process is no longer executed whenever the event occurs. Use the Subscribe step to add a new triggering event for a process.

properties.name: EventType
properties.description: Indicates whether to cancel all triggering events for the specified process or only a specific event.

properties.name: EventName
properties.description: The name of the triggering event to cancel.

properties.name: ProcessName
properties.description: The name of the process to no longer execute.

properties.name: Events
properties.description: Additional triggering events to cancel.

stepTypes.name: VisitNode
stepTypes.description: The VisitNode step may be used to execute the OnVisitingNode process of an entity that is located at a node. The executing token is held at the VisitNode step until the OnVisitingNode process is completed. Note that this step may only be used in the process logic of a Node object.

stepTypes.name: Wait
stepTypes.description: The Wait step may be used to hold a process token until one or more specified events occur.

properties.name: EventName
properties.description: The name of the event to wait for.

properties.name: EventCondition
properties.description: Optional condition that is evaluated whenever the event occurs, and which must be true in order for the wait for the event to be considered ended.

properties.name: Events
properties.description: Additional events to wait for.

properties.name: TokenWaitAction
properties.description:
The wait action to be taken by the token arriving to the Wait step.

If the action is 'WaitUntilAnyEvent', then the token will wait until any one of the specified events occurs.

If the action is 'WaitUntilAllEvents', then the token will wait until all of the specified events occur.

runSetup.name: CalendarEventsBetweenCallbacksForInteractiveRun
runSetup.description: The number of calendar events between callbacks for an interactive run.

runSetup.name: DisableRandomness
runSetup.description: Whether to disable random number generation during the run.

runSetup.name: EndTime
runSetup.description: The ending time of the simulation when RunEndType is EndingTime. For an infinite run, set RunEndType to Infinite.

runSetup.name: EndTimeUnitSubType
runSetup.description: The display unit subtype used to present EndTimeValue.

runSetup.name: EndTimeValue
runSetup.description: The run length in EndTimeUnitSubType units when RunEndType is RunLength.

runSetup.name: ExhaustiveConstraintChecking
runSetup.description: Whether to perform exhaustive constraint checking.

runSetup.name: FrameInterval
runSetup.description: The animation frame interval in simulation hours.

runSetup.name: FreezePeriodHours
runSetup.description: The time offset into the simulation at which statistics will be reset, in hours. Use zero for no warmup period.

runSetup.name: GenerateNeuralNetworkTrainingDataReplicationNumber
runSetup.description: The replication number used for random sampling when generating neural network training data.

runSetup.name: GenerateProfileReport
runSetup.description: Whether to generate a profile report for the run.

runSetup.name: Latitude
runSetup.description: The model latitude used for location-dependent behavior.

runSetup.name: LoadAction
runSetup.description: The action to take when the model is loaded.

allowedValueDescriptions.description: Do not perform an action after loading.

items.name: Off Shift Rule
items.description:
The processing rule used if the server is at the end of a shift because of its specified work schedule.

Suspend Processing - The server will immediately suspend all processing and set its resource state to 'OffShift'. Processing will resume at the start of the next shift.

Finish Work Already Started - The server will not accept any new entities but will continue processing if necessary to finish work already started. The server's resource state will be set to 'OffShiftProcessing' if processing entities during an off-shift period.

items.name: Resource Efficiency Rule
items.description:
The processing rule used to alter the rate at which work is performed if there are seized resources with defined efficiency values. The actual work duration is the planned work duration divided by the efficiency.

If the rule is ‘None’, then seized resource efficiency is ignored.

If the rule is ‘Average’, then the average seized resource efficiency value is used.

If the rule is ‘Count’, then the number of seized resources with a defined efficiency value is used.

If the rule is ‘Maximum’, then the largest efficiency value is used.

If the rule is ‘Minimum’, then the smallest efficiency value is used.

If the rule is ‘Sum’, then the sum of the seized resource efficiency values is used.

items.name: Immediately Try Seize

Setting this property to False will just insert the seize request into the server’s allocation queue. An evaluation of that queue will then be scheduled on the simulation’s current events calendar as a late priority event.

NOTE: This property setting applies only if the server has an input buffer. Otherwise, if no input buffer, then an arriving entity will always immediately try to enter the server’s processing station and seize it.

Setting this property to False will skip immediate allocation. Instead, an evaluation of the server’s allocation queue will be scheduled on the simulation’s current events calendar as a late priority event.

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourcesForProcessingResourceEfficiency
childSchema.description:
Optional value that can alter the rate at which work is performed using the seized resource(s), expressed as a fraction. The actual work duration is the planned work duration divided by the efficiency. Hence, an efficiency value greater than 1 shortens the time and a value less than 1 lengthens the time.

In the expression, use the syntax Candidate.[ObjectClass].[Attribute] to reference an attribute of the candidate resource objects (e.g., Candidate.Object.Capacity).

Set this property to blank to declare the resource efficiency as undefined.

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourcesForProcessingKeepReservedCondition
childSchema.description:
Once an entity has completed processing and released the resource requirements, an optional condition indicating whether to keep the released resource capacity reserved for possible later reuse by the same entity. Other entities will be unable to use a reserved resource unless the reservation is cancelled.

In the expression, use the syntax Candidate.[ObjectClass].[Attribute] to reference an attribute of the candidate resource object being released (e.g., Candidate.Object.Capacity).

Note that when an entity is attempting to select a resource from a group of candidates (e.g., from a list or from a population of some resource type), by default a preference will be given to select a resource that has already been reserved by that entity irrespective of the specified selection goal.

Leaving this property blank (no condition) is equivalent to entering False.

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourcesForProcessingReservationTimeout
childSchema.description:
If the keep reserved condition is true, then an optional wait time before automatically cancelling the reservation.

In the expression, use the syntax Candidate.[ObjectClass].[Attribute] to reference an attribute of resource object(s) being released (e.g., Candidate.Object.Capacity).

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourcesForProcessingSkipRequirementCondition
childSchema.description: Optional condition indicating whether to skip the resource requirement.

items.name: Off Shift Rule
items.description:
The processing rule used if a resource is at the end of a shift because of its specified work schedule.

Suspend Processing - The processing of the entity that is using the resource will be immediately suspended. Processing will resume at the start of the resource’s next shift.

Finish Work Already Started - The processing of the entity that is using the resource will be allowed to continue until finished. The resource will not be allowed to accept any new work.

Switch Resources If Possible - The processing of the entity that is using the resource will be immediately suspended. The entity will then try to resume processing as soon as possible by releasing the resource and seizing another available one that satisfies the same resource requirements.

items.name: Immediately Try Seize
items.description:
Indicates whether to immediately try seizing the resource requirements before the execution of any other simulation logic in the system and, if successful, skipping the resource allocation queues.

Setting this property to False will just insert the seize request into the resource allocation queues. An evaluation of those queues will then be scheduled on the simulation’s current events calendar as a late priority event.

Setting this property to False will skip immediate allocation. Instead, an evaluation of the resource allocation queues will be scheduled on the simulation’s current events calendar as a late priority event.

items.name: Initial Capacity
items.description:
The initial fixed capacity of this resource.

NOTE: Refer to work schedules or the user-assignable 'CurrentCapacity' state variable of a resource to dynamically change its usage capacity during a simulation run.

items.name: Ranking Rule
items.description: The static ranking rule used to order seize requests waiting to be allocated capacity of this resource.

items.name: Dynamic Selection Rule
items.description: Indicates whether this resource, when its capacity becomes available, dynamically selects the next seize request from its statically ranked allocation queue using a dynamic selection rule.

items.name: Current Size and Orientation Index
items.description: The optional name of a state variable that indexes into the object's associated symbol list, and whose value will automatically resize and orient the object to match the size and orientation of the indexed symbol.

items.name: Transfer-In Constraints
items.description:
Indicates the type of constraints used to determine whether entities can transfer into this fixed object via external input nodes.

If specified as 'Default', then the 'Can Transfer In & Out Of Objects' property setting for the entity type will determine whether an entity can perform a transfer into the object.

items.name: Transfer-Out Constraints
items.description:
Indicates the type of constraints used to determine whether entities can transfer out of this fixed object via external output nodes.

If specified as 'Default', then the 'Can Transfer In & Out Of Objects' property setting for the entity type will determine whether an entity can perform a transfer out of the object.

items.name: Expected Setup Time Expression
items.description: The expression used to get a deterministic estimation of the setup time for an entity at this fixed object.

items.name: Expected Operation Time Expression
items.description: The expression used to get a deterministic estimation of the operation time for an entity at this fixed object.

items.name: Transfer-In Time
items.description: The time required to transfer an entity into this object.

items.name: Process Type
items.description: The method used to model the processing of an entity.

items.name: Processing Time
items.description: The time required to process an entity.

items.name: Off Shift Rule
items.description:
The processing rule used if the server is at the end of a shift because of its specified work schedule.

Suspend Processing - The server will immediately suspend all processing and set its resource state to 'OffShift'. Processing will resume at the start of the next shift.

Finish Work Already Started - The server will not accept any new entities but will continue processing if necessary to finish work already started. The server's resource state will be set to 'OffShiftProcessing' if processing entities during an off-shift period.

items.name: Resource Efficiency Rule
items.description:
The processing rule used to alter the rate at which work is performed if there are seized resources with defined efficiency values. The actual work duration is the planned work duration divided by the efficiency.

If the rule is ‘None’, then seized resource efficiency is ignored.

If the rule is ‘Average’, then the average seized resource efficiency value is used.

If the rule is ‘Count’, then the number of seized resources with a defined efficiency value is used.

If the rule is ‘Maximum’, then the largest efficiency value is used.

If the rule is ‘Minimum’, then the smallest efficiency value is used.

If the rule is ‘Sum’, then the sum of the seized resource efficiency values is used.

items.name: Seize Constraint Logic
items.description:
Constraint logic used to enforce additional constraints on an entity's request to seize the server.

NOTE: This repeat group applies only if the server has an input buffer. Otherwise, if no input buffer, then this constraint logic will be ignored.

childSchema.name: SeizeConstraintLogicName
childSchema.description: The name of the Constraint Logic element used to enforce additional constraints on an entity's request to seize the server.

items.name: Immediately Try Seize
items.description:
For an arriving entity, indicates whether to immediately try seizing the server before the execution of any other simulation logic in the system and, if successful, skipping the server’s allocation queue.

Setting this property to False will just insert the seize request into the server’s allocation queue. An evaluation of that queue will then be scheduled on the simulation’s current events calendar as a late priority event.

NOTE: This property setting applies only if the server has an input buffer. Otherwise, if no input buffer, then an arriving entity will always immediately try to enter the server’s processing station and seize it.

items.name: Immediately Try Allocate When Released
items.description:
Once an entity has exited processing and released the server, indicates whether to immediately try allocating the released server capacity to waiting seize requests before the execution of any other simulation logic in the system.

Setting this property to False will skip immediate allocation. Instead, an evaluation of the server’s allocation queue will be scheduled on the simulation’s current events calendar as a late priority event.

items.description: The number of discrete entities that can be held in the buffer.

items.name: Balk Decision Type
items.description:
The method used by an entity to decide whether to balk at entering the buffer.

If the decision type is ‘Blocked’, then an entity attempting to enter the buffer will balk if the buffer is full rather than be blocked. Or, if a zero capacity buffer, the entity will balk if its attempt to transfer directly into or out of the object is blocked.

items.name: Renege Triggers
items.description: Optional time or event-driven triggers that can cause entities to abandon waiting in the buffer.

childSchema.name: InputBufferRenegeTriggerType
childSchema.description:
The type of trigger.

A time based trigger can renege an entity from the buffer once a specified wait duration expires.

An event based trigger can renege an entity from the buffer whenever a specified event occurs.

childSchema.name: InputBufferRenegeWaitDuration
childSchema.description: The wait duration until deciding whether to renege an entity from the buffer.

childSchema.name: InputBufferRenegeTriggeringEventName
childSchema.description: The name of the event whose occurrence will trigger a decision whether to renege an entity from the buffer.

childSchema.name: InputBufferRenegeDecisionType
childSchema.description: The method used when the trigger has fired to decide whether to renege an entity from the buffer.

childSchema.name: InputBufferRenegeConditionOrProbability
childSchema.description:
The renege condition or probability specified as an expression. If a probability then enter the chance of reneging as a value between 0.0 (0%) and 1.0 (100%).

NOTE: If it is necessary to check in a conditional expression whether an entity is currently waiting for a specific type of constraint, the entity ‘Queuing’ namespace provides several functions for that purpose (e.g., Entity.Queuing.IsWaitingRidePickupQueue).

childSchema.name: InputBufferRenegeNodeName
childSchema.description: Facility node location to send a reneging entity.

childSchema.name: InputBufferRenegeTriggerStartBoundary
childSchema.description: Indicates when the trigger becomes active for an entity occupying the buffer. Can be either immediately when the entity has entered the buffer or, alternatively, not until its transfer into the buffer has been ended (e.g., after a transfer-in time or any other entry related logic).

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourcesForProcessingResourceEfficiency
childSchema.description:
Optional value that can alter the rate at which work is performed using the seized resource(s), expressed as a fraction. The actual work duration is the planned work duration divided by the efficiency. Hence, an efficiency value greater than 1 shortens the time and a value less than 1 lengthens the time.

In the expression, use the syntax Candidate.[ObjectClass].[Attribute] to reference an attribute of the candidate resource objects (e.g., Candidate.Object.Capacity).

Set this property to blank to declare the resource efficiency as undefined.

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourcesForProcessingKeepReservedCondition
childSchema.description:
Once an entity has completed processing and released the resource requirements, an optional condition indicating whether to keep the released resource capacity reserved for possible later reuse by the same entity. Other entities will be unable to use a reserved resource unless the reservation is cancelled.

In the expression, use the syntax Candidate.[ObjectClass].[Attribute] to reference an attribute of the candidate resource object being released (e.g., Candidate.Object.Capacity).

Note that when an entity is attempting to select a resource from a group of candidates (e.g., from a list or from a population of some resource type), by default a preference will be given to select a resource that has already been reserved by that entity irrespective of the specified selection goal.

Leaving this property blank (no condition) is equivalent to entering False.

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourcesForProcessingReservationTimeout
childSchema.description:
If the keep reserved condition is true, then an optional wait time before automatically cancelling the reservation.

In the expression, use the syntax Candidate.[ObjectClass].[Attribute] to reference an attribute of resource object(s) being released (e.g., Candidate.Object.Capacity).

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourcesForProcessingSkipRequirementCondition
childSchema.description: Optional condition indicating whether to skip the resource requirement.

items.name: Off Shift Rule
items.description:
The processing rule used if a resource is at the end of a shift because of its specified work schedule.

Suspend Processing - The processing of the entity that is using the resource will be immediately suspended. Processing will resume at the start of the resource’s next shift.

Finish Work Already Started - The processing of the entity that is using the resource will be allowed to continue until finished. The resource will not be allowed to accept any new work.

Switch Resources If Possible - The processing of the entity that is using the resource will be immediately suspended. The entity will then try to resume processing as soon as possible by releasing the resource and seizing another available one that satisfies the same resource requirements.

Indicates the type of constraints used to determine whether entities can transfer into this fixed object via external input nodes.

items.description: The method used to model the processing of an entity.

items.name: Processing Time
items.description: The time required to process an entity.

items.name: Off Shift Rule
items.description:
The processing rule used if the server is at the end of a shift because of its specified work schedule.

Suspend Processing - The server will immediately suspend all processing and set its resource state to 'OffShift'. Processing will resume at the start of the next shift.

Finish Work Already Started - The server will not accept any new entities but will continue processing if necessary to finish work already started. The server's resource state will be set to 'OffShiftProcessing' if processing entities during an off-shift period.

items.name: Resource Efficiency Rule
items.description:
The processing rule used to alter the rate at which work is performed if there are seized resources with defined efficiency values. The actual work duration is the planned work duration divided by the efficiency.

If the rule is ‘None’, then seized resource efficiency is ignored.

If the rule is ‘Average’, then the average seized resource efficiency value is used.

If the rule is ‘Count’, then the number of seized resources with a defined efficiency value is used.

If the rule is ‘Maximum’, then the largest efficiency value is used.

If the rule is ‘Minimum’, then the smallest efficiency value is used.

If the rule is ‘Sum’, then the sum of the seized resource efficiency values is used.

items.name: Seize Constraint Logic
items.description:
Constraint logic used to enforce additional constraints on an entity's request to seize the server.

NOTE: This repeat group applies only if the server has an input buffer. Otherwise, if no input buffer, then this constraint logic will be ignored.

childSchema.name: SeizeConstraintLogicName
childSchema.description: The name of the Constraint Logic element used to enforce additional constraints on an entity's request to seize the server.

items.name: Immediately Try Seize
items.description:
For an arriving entity, indicates whether to immediately try seizing the server before the execution of any other simulation logic in the system and, if successful, skipping the server’s allocation queue.

Setting this property to False will just insert the seize request into the server’s allocation queue. An evaluation of that queue will then be scheduled on the simulation’s current events calendar as a late priority event.

NOTE: This property setting applies only if the server has an input buffer. Otherwise, if no input buffer, then an arriving entity will always immediately try to enter the server’s processing station and seize it.

items.name: Immediately Try Allocate When Released
items.description:
Once an entity has exited processing and released the server, indicates whether to immediately try allocating the released server capacity to waiting seize requests before the execution of any other simulation logic in the system.

Setting this property to False will skip immediate allocation. Instead, an evaluation of the server’s allocation queue will be scheduled on the simulation’s current events calendar as a late priority event.

items.name: Off Shift Rule
items.description:
The processing rule used if a resource is at the end of a shift because of its specified work schedule.

Suspend Processing - The processing of the entity that is using the resource will be immediately suspended. Processing will resume at the start of the resource’s next shift.

Finish Work Already Started - The processing of the entity that is using the resource will be allowed to continue until finished. The resource will not be allowed to accept any new work.

Switch Resources If Possible - The processing of the entity that is using the resource will be immediately suspended. The entity will then try to resume processing as soon as possible by releasing the resource and seizing another available one that satisfies the same resource requirements.

items.description:

Setting this property to False will just insert the seize request into the resource allocation queues. An evaluation of those queues will then be scheduled on the simulation’s current events calendar as a late priority event.

items.description: The time required to process an entity.

items.name: Off Shift Rule
items.description:
The processing rule used if the server is at the end of a shift because of its specified work schedule.

Suspend Processing - The server will immediately suspend all processing and set its resource state to 'OffShift'. Processing will resume at the start of the next shift.

Finish Work Already Started - The server will not accept any new entities but will continue processing if necessary to finish work already started. The server's resource state will be set to 'OffShiftProcessing' if processing entities during an off-shift period.

items.name: Resource Efficiency Rule
items.description:
The processing rule used to alter the rate at which work is performed if there are seized resources with defined efficiency values. The actual work duration is the planned work duration divided by the efficiency.

If the rule is ‘None’, then seized resource efficiency is ignored.

If the rule is ‘Average’, then the average seized resource efficiency value is used.

If the rule is ‘Count’, then the number of seized resources with a defined efficiency value is used.

If the rule is ‘Maximum’, then the largest efficiency value is used.

If the rule is ‘Minimum’, then the smallest efficiency value is used.

If the rule is ‘Sum’, then the sum of the seized resource efficiency values is used.

items.name: Seize Constraint Logic
items.description:
Constraint logic used to enforce additional constraints on an entity's request to seize the server.

NOTE: This repeat group applies only if the server has an input buffer. Otherwise, if no input buffer, then this constraint logic will be ignored.

childSchema.name: SeizeConstraintLogicName
childSchema.description: The name of the Constraint Logic element used to enforce additional constraints on an entity's request to seize the server.

items.name: Immediately Try Seize
items.description:
For an arriving entity, indicates whether to immediately try seizing the server before the execution of any other simulation logic in the system and, if successful, skipping the server’s allocation queue.

Setting this property to False will just insert the seize request into the server’s allocation queue. An evaluation of that queue will then be scheduled on the simulation’s current events calendar as a late priority event.

NOTE: This property setting applies only if the server has an input buffer. Otherwise, if no input buffer, then an arriving entity will always immediately try to enter the server’s processing station and seize it.

items.name: Immediately Try Allocate When Released
items.description:
Once an entity has exited processing and released the server, indicates whether to immediately try allocating the released server capacity to waiting seize requests before the execution of any other simulation logic in the system.

Setting this property to False will skip immediate allocation. Instead, an evaluation of the server’s allocation queue will be scheduled on the simulation’s current events calendar as a late priority event.

items.name: Capacity
items.description: The number of discrete entities that can be held in the buffer.

items.name: Balk Decision Type
items.description:
The method used by an entity to decide whether to balk at entering the buffer.

If the decision type is ‘Blocked’, then an entity attempting to enter the buffer will balk if the buffer is full rather than be blocked. Or, if a zero capacity buffer, the entity will balk if its attempt to transfer directly into or out of the object is blocked.

items.name: Renege Triggers
items.description: Optional time or event-driven triggers that can cause entities to abandon waiting in the buffer.

childSchema.name: InputBufferRenegeTriggerType
childSchema.description:
The type of trigger.

A time based trigger can renege an entity from the buffer once a specified wait duration expires.

An event based trigger can renege an entity from the buffer whenever a specified event occurs.

childSchema.name: InputBufferRenegeWaitDuration
childSchema.description: The wait duration until deciding whether to renege an entity from the buffer.

childSchema.name: InputBufferRenegeTriggeringEventName
childSchema.description: The name of the event whose occurrence will trigger a decision whether to renege an entity from the buffer.

childSchema.name: InputBufferRenegeDecisionType
childSchema.description: The method used when the trigger has fired to decide whether to renege an entity from the buffer.

childSchema.name: InputBufferRenegeConditionOrProbability
childSchema.description:
The renege condition or probability specified as an expression. If a probability then enter the chance of reneging as a value between 0.0 (0%) and 1.0 (100%).

NOTE: If it is necessary to check in a conditional expression whether an entity is currently waiting for a specific type of constraint, the entity ‘Queuing’ namespace provides several functions for that purpose (e.g., Entity.Queuing.IsWaitingRidePickupQueue).

childSchema.name: InputBufferRenegeNodeName
childSchema.description: Facility node location to send a reneging entity.

childSchema.name: InputBufferRenegeTriggerStartBoundary
childSchema.description: Indicates when the trigger becomes active for an entity occupying the buffer. Can be either immediately when the entity has entered the buffer or, alternatively, not until its transfer into the buffer has been ended (e.g., after a transfer-in time or any other entry related logic).

items.name: Action Type
items.description:

Add New Row - Add a new row for the entity to an output table. A reference will be automatically set to the newly added row.

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourcesForProcessingSelectionCondition
childSchema.description:
Optional condition evaluated for each candidate resource that must be true for the resource to be selected.

In the expression, use the syntax Candidate.[ObjectClass].[Attribute] to reference an attribute of the candidate resource objects (e.g., Candidate.Object.Capacity).

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourcesForProcessingResourceEfficiency
childSchema.description:
Optional value that can alter the rate at which work is performed using the seized resource(s), expressed as a fraction. The actual work duration is the planned work duration divided by the efficiency. Hence, an efficiency value greater than 1 shortens the time and a value less than 1 lengthens the time.

In the expression, use the syntax Candidate.[ObjectClass].[Attribute] to reference an attribute of the candidate resource objects (e.g., Candidate.Object.Capacity).

Set this property to blank to declare the resource efficiency as undefined.

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourcesForProcessingKeepReservedCondition
childSchema.description:
Once an entity has completed processing and released the resource requirements, an optional condition indicating whether to keep the released resource capacity reserved for possible later reuse by the same entity. Other entities will be unable to use a reserved resource unless the reservation is cancelled.

In the expression, use the syntax Candidate.[ObjectClass].[Attribute] to reference an attribute of the candidate resource object being released (e.g., Candidate.Object.Capacity).

Note that when an entity is attempting to select a resource from a group of candidates (e.g., from a list or from a population of some resource type), by default a preference will be given to select a resource that has already been reserved by that entity irrespective of the specified selection goal.

Leaving this property blank (no condition) is equivalent to entering False.

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourcesForProcessingReservationTimeout
childSchema.description:
If the keep reserved condition is true, then an optional wait time before automatically cancelling the reservation.

In the expression, use the syntax Candidate.[ObjectClass].[Attribute] to reference an attribute of resource object(s) being released (e.g., Candidate.Object.Capacity).

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourcesForProcessingSkipRequirementCondition
childSchema.description: Optional condition indicating whether to skip the resource requirement.

items.name: Off Shift Rule
items.description:
The processing rule used if a resource is at the end of a shift because of its specified work schedule.

Suspend Processing - The processing of the entity that is using the resource will be immediately suspended. Processing will resume at the start of the resource’s next shift.

Finish Work Already Started - The processing of the entity that is using the resource will be allowed to continue until finished. The resource will not be allowed to accept any new work.

Switch Resources If Possible - The processing of the entity that is using the resource will be immediately suspended. The entity will then try to resume processing as soon as possible by releasing the resource and seizing another available one that satisfies the same resource requirements.

Setting this property to False will just insert the seize request into the resource allocation queues. An evaluation of those queues will then be scheduled on the simulation’s current events calendar as a late priority event.

items.description:
The processing rule used if the server is at the end of a shift because of its specified work schedule.

Suspend Processing - The server will immediately suspend all processing and set its resource state to 'OffShift'. Processing will resume at the start of the next shift.

Finish Work Already Started - The server will not accept any new entities but will continue processing if necessary to finish work already started. The server's resource state will be set to 'OffShiftProcessing' if processing entities during an off-shift period.

items.name: Resource Efficiency Rule
items.description:
The processing rule used to alter the rate at which work is performed if there are seized resources with defined efficiency values. The actual work duration is the planned work duration divided by the efficiency.

If the rule is ‘None’, then seized resource efficiency is ignored.

If the rule is ‘Average’, then the average seized resource efficiency value is used.

If the rule is ‘Count’, then the number of seized resources with a defined efficiency value is used.

If the rule is ‘Maximum’, then the largest efficiency value is used.

If the rule is ‘Minimum’, then the smallest efficiency value is used.

If the rule is ‘Sum’, then the sum of the seized resource efficiency values is used.

NOTE: This property setting applies only if the server has an input buffer. Otherwise, if no input buffer, then an arriving entity will always immediately try to enter the server’s processing station and seize it.

items.description: The static ranking rule used to order seize requests waiting to be allocated capacity of this resource.

items.name: Dynamic Selection Rule
items.description: Indicates whether this resource, when its capacity becomes available, dynamically selects the next seize request from its statically ranked allocation queue using a dynamic selection rule.

items.description: The optional name of a state variable that indexes into the object's associated symbol list, and whose value will automatically resize and orient the object to match the size and orientation of the indexed symbol.

items.name: Transfer-In Constraints
items.description:
Indicates the type of constraints used to determine whether entities can transfer into this fixed object via external input nodes.

If specified as 'Default', then the 'Can Transfer In & Out Of Objects' property setting for the entity type will determine whether an entity can perform a transfer into the object.

items.name: Transfer-Out Constraints
items.description:
Indicates the type of constraints used to determine whether entities can transfer out of this fixed object via external output nodes.

If specified as 'Default', then the 'Can Transfer In & Out Of Objects' property setting for the entity type will determine whether an entity can perform a transfer out of the object.

items.name: Transfer-Out Condition
items.description: The condition required to allow an entity to transfer out of this fixed object via an external output node.

items.name: Expected Setup Time Expression
items.description: The expression used to get a deterministic estimation of the setup time for an entity at this fixed object.

items.name: Expected Operation Time Expression
items.description: The expression used to get a deterministic estimation of the operation time for an entity at this fixed object.

items.name: Transfer-In Time
items.description: The time required to transfer an entity into this object.

items.name: Process Type
items.description: The method used to model the processing of an entity.

items.name: Processing Time
items.description: The time required to process an entity.

items.name: Off Shift Rule
items.description:
The processing rule used if the server is at the end of a shift because of its specified work schedule.

Suspend Processing - The server will immediately suspend all processing and set its resource state to 'OffShift'. Processing will resume at the start of the next shift.

Finish Work Already Started - The server will not accept any new entities but will continue processing if necessary to finish work already started. The server's resource state will be set to 'OffShiftProcessing' if processing entities during an off-shift period.

items.name: Resource Efficiency Rule
items.description:
The processing rule used to alter the rate at which work is performed if there are seized resources with defined efficiency values. The actual work duration is the planned work duration divided by the efficiency.

If the rule is ‘None’, then seized resource efficiency is ignored.

If the rule is ‘Average’, then the average seized resource efficiency value is used.

If the rule is ‘Count’, then the number of seized resources with a defined efficiency value is used.

If the rule is ‘Maximum’, then the largest efficiency value is used.

If the rule is ‘Minimum’, then the smallest efficiency value is used.

If the rule is ‘Sum’, then the sum of the seized resource efficiency values is used.

items.name: Seize Constraint Logic
items.description:
Constraint logic used to enforce additional constraints on an entity's request to seize the server.

NOTE: This repeat group applies only if the server has an input buffer. Otherwise, if no input buffer, then this constraint logic will be ignored.

childSchema.name: SeizeConstraintLogicName
childSchema.description: The name of the Constraint Logic element used to enforce additional constraints on an entity's request to seize the server.

items.name: Immediately Try Seize
items.description:
For an arriving entity, indicates whether to immediately try seizing the server before the execution of any other simulation logic in the system and, if successful, skipping the server’s allocation queue.

Setting this property to False will just insert the seize request into the server’s allocation queue. An evaluation of that queue will then be scheduled on the simulation’s current events calendar as a late priority event.

NOTE: This property setting applies only if the server has an input buffer. Otherwise, if no input buffer, then an arriving entity will always immediately try to enter the server’s processing station and seize it.

items.name: Immediately Try Allocate When Released
items.description:
Once an entity has exited processing and released the server, indicates whether to immediately try allocating the released server capacity to waiting seize requests before the execution of any other simulation logic in the system.

Setting this property to False will skip immediate allocation. Instead, an evaluation of the server’s allocation queue will be scheduled on the simulation’s current events calendar as a late priority event.

items.name: Balk Decision Type
items.description:
The method used by an entity to decide whether to balk at entering the buffer.

If the decision type is ‘Blocked’, then an entity attempting to enter the buffer will balk if the buffer is full rather than be blocked. Or, if a zero capacity buffer, the entity will balk if its attempt to transfer directly into or out of the object is blocked.

items.name: Renege Triggers
items.description: Optional time or event-driven triggers that can cause entities to abandon waiting in the buffer.

childSchema.name: InputBufferRenegeTriggerType
childSchema.description:
The type of trigger.

A time based trigger can renege an entity from the buffer once a specified wait duration expires.

An event based trigger can renege an entity from the buffer whenever a specified event occurs.

childSchema.name: InputBufferRenegeWaitDuration
childSchema.description: The wait duration until deciding whether to renege an entity from the buffer.

childSchema.name: InputBufferRenegeTriggeringEventName
childSchema.description: The name of the event whose occurrence will trigger a decision whether to renege an entity from the buffer.

childSchema.name: InputBufferRenegeDecisionType
childSchema.description: The method used when the trigger has fired to decide whether to renege an entity from the buffer.

childSchema.name: InputBufferRenegeConditionOrProbability
childSchema.description:
The renege condition or probability specified as an expression. If a probability then enter the chance of reneging as a value between 0.0 (0%) and 1.0 (100%).

NOTE: If it is necessary to check in a conditional expression whether an entity is currently waiting for a specific type of constraint, the entity ‘Queuing’ namespace provides several functions for that purpose (e.g., Entity.Queuing.IsWaitingRidePickupQueue).

childSchema.name: InputBufferRenegeNodeName
childSchema.description: Facility node location to send a reneging entity.

childSchema.name: InputBufferRenegeTriggerStartBoundary
childSchema.description: Indicates when the trigger becomes active for an entity occupying the buffer. Can be either immediately when the entity has entered the buffer or, alternatively, not until its transfer into the buffer has been ended (e.g., after a transfer-in time or any other entry related logic).

childSchema.description: The rule used to select a resource object from multiple candidates.

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourcesForProcessingSelectionValueExpression
childSchema.description:
The expression used to get the value for each candidate resource.

In the expression, use the syntax Candidate.[ObjectClass].[Attribute] to reference an attribute of the candidate resource objects (e.g., Candidate.Object.Capacity).

childSchema.description: Indicates whether a move to a specified node will be requested from the seized resource(s). Processing will not be able to continue until arrival of the resources at the node location.

childSchema.description: The name of the destination node that the seized resource(s) will be requested to move to.

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourcesForProcessingNumberOfResources
childSchema.description: The number of individual resource objects to seize capacity units of.

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourcesForProcessingUnitsPerResource
childSchema.description:
The number of capacity units to seize per candidate resource.

In the expression, use the syntax Candidate.[ObjectClass].[Attribute] to reference an attribute of the candidate resource objects (e.g., Candidate.Object.Capacity).

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourcesForProcessingSelectionCondition
childSchema.description:
Optional condition evaluated for each candidate resource that must be true for the resource to be selected.

In the expression, use the syntax Candidate.[ObjectClass].[Attribute] to reference an attribute of the candidate resource objects (e.g., Candidate.Object.Capacity).

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourcesForProcessingResourceEfficiency
childSchema.description:
Optional value that can alter the rate at which work is performed using the seized resource(s), expressed as a fraction. The actual work duration is the planned work duration divided by the efficiency. Hence, an efficiency value greater than 1 shortens the time and a value less than 1 lengthens the time.

In the expression, use the syntax Candidate.[ObjectClass].[Attribute] to reference an attribute of the candidate resource objects (e.g., Candidate.Object.Capacity).

Set this property to blank to declare the resource efficiency as undefined.

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourcesForProcessingKeepReservedCondition
childSchema.description:
Once an entity has completed processing and released the resource requirements, an optional condition indicating whether to keep the released resource capacity reserved for possible later reuse by the same entity. Other entities will be unable to use a reserved resource unless the reservation is cancelled.

In the expression, use the syntax Candidate.[ObjectClass].[Attribute] to reference an attribute of the candidate resource object being released (e.g., Candidate.Object.Capacity).

Note that when an entity is attempting to select a resource from a group of candidates (e.g., from a list or from a population of some resource type), by default a preference will be given to select a resource that has already been reserved by that entity irrespective of the specified selection goal.

Leaving this property blank (no condition) is equivalent to entering False.

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourcesForProcessingReservationTimeout
childSchema.description:
If the keep reserved condition is true, then an optional wait time before automatically cancelling the reservation.

In the expression, use the syntax Candidate.[ObjectClass].[Attribute] to reference an attribute of resource object(s) being released (e.g., Candidate.Object.Capacity).

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourcesForProcessingSkipRequirementCondition
childSchema.description: Optional condition indicating whether to skip the resource requirement.

items.name: Off Shift Rule
items.description:
The processing rule used if a resource is at the end of a shift because of its specified work schedule.

Suspend Processing - The processing of the entity that is using the resource will be immediately suspended. Processing will resume at the start of the resource’s next shift.

Finish Work Already Started - The processing of the entity that is using the resource will be allowed to continue until finished. The resource will not be allowed to accept any new work.

Switch Resources If Possible - The processing of the entity that is using the resource will be immediately suspended. The entity will then try to resume processing as soon as possible by releasing the resource and seizing another available one that satisfies the same resource requirements.

items.name: Must Simultaneously Seize
items.description: If multiple resources are required, indicates whether all of the resources must be available before any can be seized.

items.name: Immediately Try Seize
items.description:
Indicates whether to immediately try seizing the resource requirements before the execution of any other simulation logic in the system and, if successful, skipping the resource allocation queues.

Setting this property to False will just insert the seize request into the resource allocation queues. An evaluation of those queues will then be scheduled on the simulation’s current events calendar as a late priority event.

items.name: Immediately Try Allocate When Released

Once an entity has completed processing and released the resource requirements, indicates whether to immediately try allocating the released resource capacity to waiting seize requests before the execution of any other simulation logic in the system.

Setting this property to False will skip immediate allocation. Instead, an evaluation of the resource allocation queues will be scheduled on the simulation’s current events calendar as a late priority event.

childSchema.description: The name of the object list from which to select the resource object(s) to release.

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourceReleasesAfterProcessingQuantityType
childSchema.description:
Indicates the type of resource quantity to release.

Specific – Is the exact quantities entered in the Number Of Objects and Units Per Object properties.

All – Is all currently seized resources of the specified resource type.

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourceReleasesAfterProcessingNumberOfResources
childSchema.description: The number of individual resource objects to release capacity units of.

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourceReleasesAfterProcessingUnitsPerResource
childSchema.description:
The number of capacity units to release per candidate resource.

In the expression, use the syntax Candidate.[ObjectClass].[Attribute] to reference an attribute of the candidate resource objects (e.g., Candidate.Object.Capacity).

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourceReleasesAfterProcessingReleaseOrder
childSchema.description: The order in which to release the resources that have been seized by the entity.

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourceReleasesAfterProcessingSelectionCondition
childSchema.description:
Optional condition evaluated for each seized resource that must be true for the resource to be selected.

In the expression, use the syntax Candidate.[ObjectClass].[Attribute] to reference an attribute of the candidate resource objects (e.g., Candidate.Object.Capacity).

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourceReleasesAfterProcessingKeepReservedCondition
childSchema.description:
Optional condition indicating whether to keep the released resource capacity reserved for possible later reuse by the same entity. Other entities will be unable to use a reserved resource unless the reservation is cancelled.

In the expression, use the syntax Candidate.[ObjectClass].[Attribute] to reference an attribute of the candidate resource object(s) being released (e.g., Candidate.Object.Capacity).

Note that when an entity is attempting to select a resource from a group of candidates (e.g., from a list or from a population of some resource type), by default a preference will be given to select a resource that has already been reserved by that owner irrespective of the specified selection goal.

Leaving this property blank (no condition) is equivalent to entering False.

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourceReleasesAfterProcessingReservationTimeout
childSchema.description:
If the keep reserved condition is true, then an optional wait time before automatically cancelling the reservation.

In the expression, use the syntax Candidate.[ObjectClass].[Attribute] to reference an attribute of the resource object(s) being released (e.g., Candidate.Object.Capacity).

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourceReleasesAfterProcessingOnReleasedProcess
childSchema.description: Optional process to be executed when a resource is released.

childSchema.name: SecondaryResourceReleasesAfterProcessingSkipReleaseCondition
childSchema.description: Optional condition indicating whether to skip the release requirement.

items.name: Immediately Try Allocate When Released
items.description:
Indicates whether to immediately try allocating the released resource capacity to waiting seize requests before the execution of any other simulation logic in the system.

Setting this property to False will skip immediate allocation. Instead, an evaluation of the resource allocation queues will be scheduled on the simulation’s current events calendar as a late priority event.

processes.VSM_OnProductionRelease:
<Process Name="VSM_OnProductionRelease" ShowAsUserExecutableProcess="False" BeginStepID="2" Scope="Public">
  <Properties>
    <Property Name="ReportStatistics">True</Property>
    <Property Name="TriggeringEventName">Output@Source_ProductionRelease.Entered</Property>
    <Property Name="TriggeringEventCondition"></Property>
    <Property Name="ImmediatelyExecuteCondition"></Property>
    <Property Name="TokenClassName">Token</Property>
    <Property Name="TokenActionOnAssociatedObjectDestroyed">ContinueProcess</Property>
    <Property Name="TokenActionOnAssociatedObjectTransferRequested">ContinueProcess</Property>
    <Property Name="InitiallyEnabled">True</Property>
    <Property Name="AllowStepTrace">True</Property>
  </Properties>
  <Steps>
    <Step Type="Assign" Name="累计释放件数" ID="2">
      <Properties>
        <Property Name="StateVariableName">
          <Value>VSM_ReleaseSequence</Value>
        </Property>
        <Property Name="NewValue">VSM_ReleaseSequence + 20</Property>
      </Properties>
      <Exit Name="Exit" Type="Primary" NextID="3" />
    </Step>
    <Step Type="Assign" Name="确定产品类型" ID="3">
      <Properties>
        <Property Name="StateVariableName">
          <Value>ModelEntity.VSM_ProductTypeState</Value>
        </Property>
        <Property Name="NewValue">Math.If(VSM_ReleaseSequence - 9200*Math.Floor((VSM_ReleaseSequence-1)/9200) <= 6000,"Left","Right")</Property>
      </Properties>
      <Exit Name="Exit" Type="Primary" NextID="4" />
    </Step>
    <Step Type="Assign" Name="记录释放时刻" ID="4">
      <Properties>
        <Property Name="StateVariableName">
          <Value>ModelEntity.VSM_ReleaseTimeHoursState</Value>
        </Property>
        <Property Name="NewValue">TimeNow</Property>
      </Properties>
      <Exit Name="Exit" Type="Primary" NextID="5" />
    </Step>
    <Step Type="Assign" Name="记录生产批次" ID="5">
      <Properties>
        <Property Name="StateVariableName">
          <Value>ModelEntity.VSM_ProductionBatchState</Value>
        </Property>
        <Property Name="NewValue">Math.If(VSM_ReleaseSequence - 9200*Math.Floor((VSM_ReleaseSequence-1)/9200) <= 6000,"L_6000_Batch","R_3200_Batch")</Property>
      </Properties>
      <Exit Name="Exit" Type="Primary" NextID="6" />
    </Step>
    <Step Type="Assign" Name="累计Left释放件数" ID="6">
      <Properties>
        <Property Name="StateVariableName">
          <Value>VSM_LeftReleasedCount</Value>
        </Property>
        <Property Name="NewValue">VSM_LeftReleasedCount + Math.If(VSM_ReleaseSequence - 9200*Math.Floor((VSM_ReleaseSequence-1)/9200) <= 6000,20,0)</Property>
      </Properties>
      <Exit Name="Exit" Type="Primary" NextID="7" />
    </Step>
    <Step Type="Assign" Name="累计Right释放件数" ID="7">
      <Properties>
        <Property Name="StateVariableName">
          <Value>VSM_RightReleasedCount</Value>
        </Property>
        <Property Name="NewValue">VSM_RightReleasedCount + Math.If(VSM_ReleaseSequence - 9200*Math.Floor((VSM_ReleaseSequence-1)/9200) <= 6000,0,20)</Property>
      </Properties>
      <Exit Name="Exit" Type="Primary" NextID="8" />
    </Step>
    <Step Type="Assign" Name="记录实体件数和托盘序号" ID="8">
      <Properties>
        <Property Name="StateVariableName">
          <Value>ModelEntity.VSM_QuantityState</Value>
        </Property>
        <Property Name="NewValue">20</Property>
        <Property Name="Assignments">
          <Rows>
            <Properties>
              <Property Name="AssignmentsStateVariableName">
                <Value>ModelEntity.VSM_TrayIDState</Value>
              </Property>
              <Property Name="AssignmentsNewValue">Math.Floor((VSM_ReleaseSequence-1)/20)+1</Property>
              <Property Name="AssignmentsSkipAssignmentCondition"></Property>
            </Properties>
          </Rows>
        </Property>
      </Properties>
    </Step>
  </Steps>
</Process>

<Process Name="VSM_OnShipment" BeginStepID="2" Scope="Public" Description="实体到达Sink_Shipping即将销毁时，读取实体代表的工件数量并累计到加权交付件数；输入单位件，仿真初始化时全局计数为0。">
